name: Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune
tagline: The East Coast home of Marine expeditionary forces, on the North Carolina coast at Jacksonville.
_note: First Marine Corps base in the app. Coastal NC (Jacksonville, Onslow County). Facts verified from official sources (lejeune.marines.mil, MilitaryINSTALLATIONS, camplejeunefamilyhousing.com, DeCA/MCX, Wikipedia for corroborated headline facts). BAH MHA NC178 (Camp Lejeune) via the bah_rates single source of truth. Corrected 2026-11-09 from the website-page research (Base Guides/page-builder/research/lejeune-facts.md): there ARE DoD schools (7, pre-K to 12, Lejeune High School); housing is Hunt Military Communities (bought AMCC from Lendlease, Oct 2024) and Liberty Military Housing (Heroes Manor), 5,204 units; 156,000 acres; gate hours from the Provost Marshal page; Onslow reappraisal delayed to tax year 2027. Removed unverified claims (plentiful housing, lowest cost of living, School of Infantry/MARSOC/Combat Service Support Schools wording). sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Camp Lejeune is the East Coast's home of Marine expeditionary forces. It is home to the II Marine Expeditionary Force (II MEF), the 2nd Marine Division, and the 2nd Marine Logistics Group, the ground, logistics, and command backbone of the Atlantic Marine force.
The base covers 156,000 acres along the New River and the Atlantic, with 11 miles of beach used for amphibious training.

sections.title: On Base or Off? The Camp Lejeune School and Tax Decision

data.subtitle: The first choice here is on base or off. On base, active-duty families' children attend DoD schools from pre-K through high school; off base, your address sets the school system, the county tax and the gate you use.
intro: Camp Lejeune runs seven DoD schools, ending at Lejeune High School, for families who live on base. Off base, most towns are served by Onslow County Schools, where 9 of 40 graded schools were rated low-performing in 2025-26 and the Class of 2026 graduated at 91.6%. Cape Carteret is in Carteret County and Hampstead in Pender County, each with its own schools.

Property tax is changing too. Onslow's 2026 reappraisal raised residential values about 40% on average, and state law delays using the new values until the 2027 tax year, so check what a home will be assessed at, not just this year's bill.

recommendations.advice: DoD schools pre-K to 12. Waits posted in October 2026 ran from 0 to 1 month in some E-1 to E-5 neighborhoods to 12 to 14 months for some E-6 to E-9 homes.
Jacksonville is about 13 minutes from Naval Medical Center Camp Lejeune with no traffic; Hubert about 15.
Swansboro (Onslow) and Cape Carteret (Carteret) are about 26 to 35 minutes away; Sneads Ferry and Holly Ridge about 42 to 43 via US 17. Check which gate you would use and when it is open.
Active-duty families off base can apply for a DoD school seat if space allows (applications April 1 to October 31), with no bus.

source.label: Camp Lejeune DoD schools; NC DPI 2025-26; Onslow County revaluation

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Open 24 hours: Holcomb (the Main Gate), Wilson, Sneads Ferry, Stone Bay, Camp Johnson and Midway Park. Piney Green is open weekdays only, and the Triangle Outpost Gate on NC 172 in Hubert opens only at weekday rush hours; both close on weekends and federal holidays.

Under current heightened security every adult in the car is checked, and guests 18 and over need a REAL ID or a U.S. passport. The Visitor Center at Wilson Gate (Building TT-13) is open weekdays 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.
Gate hours and visitor requirements change, so confirm the current details on the Provost Marshal's page before you go.

source.label: MCB Camp Lejeune Provost Marshal's Office (official)

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: On-base family housing is privatized. Hunt Military Communities bought Atlantic Marine Corps Communities in 2024 and runs most neighborhoods, and Liberty Military Housing runs Heroes Manor. Military OneSource counts 5,204 homes across both partners.

Military Housing Office: (910) 450-1628, toll-free 1-866-360-3775, TT-43 Inchon Street, Tarawa Terrace. Waits posted in October 2026 ran from 0 to 1 month to 12 to 14 months depending on rank, neighborhood and bedrooms.

source.label: Camp Lejeune Military Housing Office (official); Hunt Companies

sections.title: Schools
data: Camp Lejeune has seven DoD schools (DoDEA, which now also calls itself DoWEA) for families who live on base, from pre-K through grade 12 at Lejeune High School.

Off base, the county sets the school system: Onslow County Schools in most towns (9 of 40 graded schools low-performing in 2025-26; Class of 2026 graduation 91.6%), Carteret County Schools in Cape Carteret, and Pender County Schools in Hampstead. Active-duty families off base can apply for a DoD seat if space allows, with no bus.
Confirm the school for any address with the School Liaison at 910-449-9915.

source.label: Camp Lejeune Schools (DoDEA); NC DPI 2025-26 results

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves, and the answer is mostly about how long you'll be here and how steady the local market is.
rent: Your tour is short (about two years or less) or your orders feel uncertain.
You want time to learn the area before committing to a neighborhood.
You'd rather not gamble on resale timing when you PCS out.
Your BAH comfortably covers rent in the areas you'd consider.
buy: You expect to be here three or more years.
You want to use your VA loan and build equity instead of paying rent.
The market is steady and you could rent the home out later if needed.
You've found a neighborhood and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer. Buyers in Onslow and Pender should plan for higher assessed values from the 2027 tax year, and coastal buyers should check flood zone and flood history on the seller's disclosure. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, weigh your tour length, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a new duty station is mostly logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) for a limited number of days while you house-hunt.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Start with the Housing Office
steps.text: Check on-base availability and get the housing office's read on off-base neighborhoods before you sign anything.

steps.title: Register your vehicle and sort access
steps.text: Handle base access and vehicle registration, and learn the visitor-pass process for guests. Bring your registration and insurance.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Contact the base DoD schools if you will live on base, or your county's school system if not, and bring records and immunizations. The School Liaison (910-449-9915) can help.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE enrollment so you can be seen at Naval Medical Center Camp Lejeune or network providers.

data.a: It's the home base of II Marine Expeditionary Force, the 2nd Marine Division and the 2nd Marine Logistics Group, plus other combat units and support commands.
Yes. Seven DoD schools serve families who live on base, from pre-K through grade 12 at Lejeune High School. Off base, your county sets the school system.
Holcomb (the Main Gate), Wilson, Sneads Ferry, Stone Bay, Camp Johnson and Midway Park. Piney Green and the Triangle Outpost Gate keep weekday hours only.
Hunt Military Communities, which bought Atlantic Marine Corps Communities in 2024, and Liberty Military Housing at Heroes Manor. Call the Military Housing Office at (910) 450-1628.
Camp Lejeune is MHA NC178. Use the calculator above for your grade.
